/**
 * \brief Return the pointer to an initialized result iterator.
 */
int db_get_row(db_query_res_t *res, int index, db_row_t *row) {
    if (res == NULL || row == NULL) {
        return 1;
    }
    if (index < 0 || index >= res->size) {
        return 1;
    }
    *row = res->rows[index];
    return 0;
}

/**
 * \brief Free a result set.
 */
void db_free_res(db_query_res_t *res) {
    int i, j;
    if (res == NULL) {
        return;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < res->size; i++) {
        for (j = 0; j < res->n_cols; j++) {
            free(res->rows[i][j]);
        }
        free(res->rows[i]);
    }
    free(res->rows);
    free(res->fields);
    free(res);
}

    }
    for (i = 0; i < res->n_cols; i++) {
        printf("%s\t", res->fields[i]);

The issue you're facing is a classic mobile web development challenge. On many mobile browsers (especially Safari on iPhone and Chrome on Android), the address bar and navigation toolbars change size as you scroll, or they cover part of the `100vh` height, causing buttons at the bottom to disappear or be partially cut off.

Since you asked for suggestions without modifying the code yet, here are the best professional solutions to fix this:

### 1. Switch to Dynamic Viewport Units (`dvh`)
Instead of using `100vh` (which is often "static" and ignores browser toolbars), use `100dvh` (Dynamic Viewport Height).
*   **Why:** `dvh` automatically adjusts its value as the browser UI (like the address bar) expands or collapses. It is the modern standard for "full-screen" mobile apps.

### 2. Handle "Safe Area" Insets
Phones with "notches" or home indicator bars (like iPhone 12/13/14/15/16) require extra padding at the bottom so buttons don't overlap with the system's "swipe-up" line.
*   **Suggestion:** Use CSS environment variables like `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom);`. This ensures the buttons are pushed up just enough to be safely clickable.

### 3. Change the Footer Positioning from `absolute` to `sticky` or Flexbox
Currently, your footer is `absolute bottom-0`. In some mobile rendering engines, if the parent container's height is calculated slightly wrong, an absolute element can "fall" off the bottom of the visible screen.
*   **Suggestion:** Make the main container a Flexbox (`flex flex-col h-screen`) and keep the footer as a standard block at the end of the flex column. This forces the browser to calculate the footer's position relative to the actual visible space.

### 4. Add "Bottom Breathing Room" (Padding)
The scrollable area (`main`) needs a large bottom padding (e.g., `pb-32`) to ensure that when a user scrolls to the very end of the chat, the last message isn't hidden behind the floating microphone button.

### 5. Use `min-h-screen` instead of `h-full`
On the outermost wrapper, using `min-h-[100dvh]` ensures the app always takes up at least the full visible screen, but allows it to grow if the mobile browser behaves unexpectedly.

**Summary Recommendation:**
The most effective "quick fix" for stability is **replacing `100vh` with `100dvh`** and adding **Safe Area Insets**. This is how world-class mobile web apps (like the mobile versions of Twitter or WhatsApp) handle this exact problem.

The Gemini Live (Multimodal Audio) API is billed at a premium rate per minute of audio processed.

Currently, the Google Search tool is "Always Available," which can sometimes lead the model to search for trivial things, incurring a cost of ~$0.03 per turn.

### 3. Client-Side "Silence Detection" & Auto-Stop
Rural environments are often noisy (markets, children, cattle). The AI processes this background noise as active audio tokens.
*   **The Change:** Implement a logic that monitors the microphone's volume levels. If no voice is detected for 10 seconds, the app should automatically stop the recording and disconnect the session.
*   **Why:** This stops "token leakage" where you are paying for the AI to listen to a noisy room.

### 4. Context Pruning (Memory Management)
In long conversations, the model "remembers" everything, sending all previous messages back to the server with every new sentence.
*   **The Change:** Limit the "Short-Term Memory" to only the last 4 exchanges. Store the rest in the local device database (IndexedDB) for the user to read, but don't send it to the AI.
*   **Why:** Reduces the "Input Token" count significantly in long conversations.

### 5. Local FAQ / Static Responses
Users often ask the same basic questions (e.g., "What is this app?", "Who made this?", "Help").

Every second of audio the AI speaks costs money.
*   **The Change:** Update the System Instruction to strictly limit responses to 2-3 sentences unless the user asks for more detail.
*   **Why:** Half the audio duration equals half the output cost.

**Summary:** By moving from a "Live Multimodal" model to a "Text-Prompt + Selective Search" model, you can scale to thousands of users with a much smaller budget.

### **The Calculation (Per 1,000 Interactions)**

| Metric | **Long Responses** (~45 sec) | **Short Responses** (~15 sec) | **Savings** |
